title: sre-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-26
content:
On-call scratchpad - 2026-03-26
Owner: Amanda Khan (eng-sre)
Shift: 09:00 - 17:00 PT
Collaborators pinged: Ben, Lena

Summary
- Quiet morning until ~10:14 UTC when we received a spike in 5xx from hosted-api (customer-facing endpoints). PagerDuty: 1 page (high).
- Incident resolved by 10:40 UTC via rolling restart of a problematic pool (rwd-serving-prod-pool-7). Root cause: memory leak in model runner after recent kernel upgrade + larger batch sizes for a specific tenant.

Timeline / notes
- 10:12 UTC: Alert fired - hosted-api 5xx rate > 1% for 5m (grafana alert hosted-api-5xx-rate). PD page: INC-2026-042.
- 10:14 UTC: I joined the channel #oncall-incident, grabbed logs from gateway (gw-prod-03) and started tailing runtime logs on rwd-serving-prod-pool-7. Noticed OOM-kill events and repeated Java/C++ aborts in model-runner.
- 10:18 UTC: Scaled down batch size override for tenant-42 (temp) via feature-flag (ffctl) to reduce per-request memory.
- 10:25 UTC: Decided to roll pool: cordon + drain rwd-serving-prod-pool-7, restarted nodes.
- 10:35 UTC: Nodes back, traffic restored, 5xx rate dropped below threshold.
- 10:40 UTC: Declared resolved on PD after monitoring for 15m and ensuring no recurrence.

Immediate follow-ups (action items)
- [ ] Create postmortem draft for INC-2026-042 (owner: Amanda) - due 2026-03-29. Link to incident channel and logs. (Jira: SRE-2026)
- [ ] Open infra ticket to revert/validate kernel changes on GPU fleets and run extended soak tests (owner: Ben) - INFRA-7890.
- [ ] Add memory oom detection to model-runner healthcheck so pool autoscaler can react earlier (owner: Lena) - PR needed in /serving-runtime repo.
- [ ] Add temporary guardrail in ramp rules to prevent tenant-42 from autoscaling batch sizes beyond X until we have memory profiling (owner: product + runtime).

Runbook TODOs (notes to improve)
- Serving runtime OOM runbook misses step: how to temporarily reduce per-tenant batch-size via ffctl (I had to improvise). Add snip:
  - ffctl set tenant-override tenant-42 batch_size 8
  - wait 60s for effect, monitor kv-cache and mem usage
- Add explicit Grafana dashboard panels for resident set size per process on GPU nodes (currently only aggregated host mem).
- Add a quick checklist for draining nodes that includes verifying KV cache flush and tombstone windows (we briefly saw spike in latency during drain).

Metrics observed
- 5xx rate: peaked at 2.7% at 10:16 UTC, returned to ~0.06% by 10:33 UTC.
- p95 latency increased from 120ms -> 540ms during the spike.
- GPU mem usage on rwd-serving-prod-pool-7 nodes showed a steady climb leading to OOMs (approx +800MB over 30m).

Logs / snippets (copied from node)
- model-runner: "[ERR] Allocation failed: requested 512MB beyond available workspace" repeated 14x before kernel OOM kill.
- kernel messages: "Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (model-runner) score 987"

Paging & noise
- Received one legitimate page at 10:12. No other flurry of noisy alerts. Good signal-to-noise for this incident.

Hand-off notes for next on-call (17:00 PT)
- Monitor INC-2026-042 postmortem progress and ensure infra ticket INFRA-7890 is assigned.
- Watch for any increase in p95 latency for hosted-api and any OOM signs on pools rwd-serving-prod-pool-6/7/8.
- If similar OOMs recur, escalate to runtime oncall (pager: runtime-lead) and consider immediate rollback of recent kernel upgrade (coord with release-eng).

Longer-term follow-ups (backlog)
- Investigate memory leak hypothesis in model-runner (heap vs native allocation) - assign to applied-ml + serving-runtime team.
- Add automated nightly soak for newly-upgraded kernels on a canary pool with simulated multi-tenant load. (chore: infra-soak)
- Revisit autoscaler policy: include per-pod mem headroom as a scaling signal rather than only CPU/throughput.

Quick TODO (my personal)
- [ ] Draft postmortem skeleton and share with Ben for review.
- [ ] Add ffctl snippet to runbook and open PR to confluence runbook page.
- [ ] Capture heap/profile output next time we repro (add to runbook to collect /tmp/prof-*.tgz).

Questions / unknowns to resolve
- Did tenant-42 recent client change increase seq length? (ask product/solutions) - unresolved.
- Kernel change: exact commit that landed on 03/24 - need release-eng confirmation.

Useful links
- Incident channel: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234INCIDENT
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Serving+Runtime+OOM+Runbook
- Infra ticket: INFRA-7890
- Jira: SRE-2026

Random notes / scratch (stuff I typed during the shift)
- If we can get per-tenant memory metrics into trace/span, easier to correlate later.
- Consider a memory-based throttling circuit breaker for model-runner (very conservative).
- Remember to link PR for healthcheck to postmortem before circulating.

End of shift quick summary (for #oncall-ops)
- Incident: INC-2026-042 - Hosting API 5xx spike due to OOMs on serving pool. Resolved via batch size override + rolling restart. Follow-ups created (SRE-2026, INFRA-7890).

-- Amanda
